items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Erwin (Vany) Hinder, the tenor and clarinet man and I had been together in a club called "Cave de la Huchatte" often.

ctx.x: It was short notice for me but there are certain musicians that I engage to do galas and concerts quite regular, and it was lucky for me that they were free and willing to make the trip with me. And it was also a blessing for me, because I did not have to spend hours rehearsing with a strange group, although I've done that many times, and shall probablu have to do it many more times. I play the game as it should be played. It was naturally more agreeable to have musicians with me that knew what I would do and…

Pierre Sim, bassist, Alain Fougeret, pianist, worked with me often. Michael Silva, an ex-drummer of Sammy Davis Jr., had also been an a few jobs with me. Erwin (Vany) Hinder, the tenor and clarinet man and I had been together in a club called "Cave de la Huchatte" often. Sim and Alain were French, Vany-Swiss, Michael and myself were American, so the group was international.

We arrived in Algiers the 8th of April and left for Oran, a city in Algeria, the next morning at 7:30. We were obliged to take a plane to Oran at that hour because there were only two flights there every day, one every morning, and one in the evening. When we arrived in Oran, we had to wait for hours to get rooms, because no reservations had been made as it should have been. We found out also that no publicity had been made for our concert.
